title: A visitor and a flower
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: Both partners benefit in the stated interaction, an example of mutualism. Actual costs and benefits can depend on the species and context.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: A bee gains nectar and, in this example, pollinates the flower, improving the plant's reproduction. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Bee and Flower, in that order? Bee: +; Flower: +. Both partners benefit in the stated interaction, an example of mutualism. Actual costs and benefits can depend on the species and context.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Bee–Flower interaction as stated in the lesson? Both partners benefit in the stated interaction, an example of mutualism. Actual costs and benefits can depend on the species and context.
